sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet 7 Status
sections.summary: Devnet 7 is stable; Erigon onboarding is the last client, Death Star and malicious Prysm node adding chaos testing.
sections.body:
- Dust has settled on Glamsterdam Devnet 7; network performing well.
- Erigon is in the process of onboarding as the last client; Grandine was added before the weekend.
  - Erigon and Grandine will have fewer validators until more deposits come in, so they may propose less.
- Death Star (a modified version of Lodestar that acts maliciously) has been added to Devnet 7 for more chaos.
- Prysm/Erigon combo missing slots on Dora; likely still syncing and not fully caught up yet.
- Malicious Prysm node updated by PandaOps; pending review from Aussie team before activation.
  - Will introduce more degrees of freedom than Death Star this week.
- Stefan plans to incrementally add more testing and chaos scenarios to Devnet 7, but will avoid crashing it since it was made available to a broader audience.

sections.heading: Devnet 8 Planning
sections.summary: Devnet 8 targeted for next week or the week after; Devnet 9 envisioned as a non-finality-focused network within the month.
sections.body:
- Target for Devnet 8 is next week or the week after; no rush given holidays, pending repricing EIP changes, and benchmarking still needing time.
- Goal: smooth fork transition with all clients on Devnet 8.
- Devnet 9 envisioned as a non-finality-focused network, ideally within the next month.
- At least one more fork transition test desired on Devnet 8 before moving to testnets.
- Discv5 only for EL on Devnet 8: Csaba raised the proposal; no objections.
  - Csaba will do a small code test on the testnet before the DevNet to confirm.
  - Dustin confirmed Nimbus EL supports discv5 and would prefer discv5-only.
- QUIC confirmed enabled on Devnet 7; will carry forward.

sections.heading: Fork Transition Bugs and Performance
sections.summary: CL clients hit SSZ stable container issues at fork transition due to large validator set; 10-20% performance regression confirmed across clients.
sections.body:
- Main EL issues: gas accounting inconsistencies; nothing out of the ordinary.
- CL surprise: SSZ stable containers at fork transition were problematic due to the large validator set size (many exiting validators).
- Lodestar bug: spread operator blowing the stack on large Merkle trees (hundreds of thousands of nodes).
  - Not caught in small-tree testing; only surfaced at devnet scale.
- Stable containers performance impact: 10-20% slower across clients.
  - Grandine confirmed significant slowdown in some places; optimization needed.
  - Teku confirmed slower implementation compared to non-progressive version; still manageable but optimization round needed, especially for larger data structures.
  - Further benchmarking on bigger data structures still required before mainnet.

sections.heading: EIP Staging and SFI Status
sections.summary: All Devnet 7 EIPs appear to satisfy SFI criteria per EIP-7723; official ratification deferred to the ACD call on Thursday.
sections.body:
- All Devnet 7 EIPs appear to satisfy the four SFI criteria defined in [EIP-7723](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7723).
- PandaOps team comfortable with SFI move; similar sentiment from EL teams.
- Decision: official SFI ratification can only happen at ACD-E/C; proposed for the next ACD call on Thursday.
- EIP-7773 (Meta EIP for Glamsterdam upgrade): proposed move to Review status; no objections raised.
  - Authors asked to add PRs to EIP editing office hours tomorrow for merge before Thursday's ACD call.

sections.heading: BAL JSON RPC Alignment
sections.summary: BAL-specific JSON RPC responses diverge across clients; clients asked to review HackMD summary and align by Devnet 8.
sections.body:
- JSON RPC responses for Block Access List (BAL) methods differ across clients (error codes, empty lists vs. omission, access list format).
- Toni summarized all divergence points in a HackMD document; clients asked to review.
  - PR raised against execution-APIs to clarify all points of divergence.
  - Link shared in [BAL Discord channel](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1364000387195076608/1527979143881429153).
- Chase is working on a JSON RPC test suite; Stefan suggested coordinating to add BAL-specific access list tests there.
- Target: alignment across clients by Devnet 8.
- Sub-call traces: Dragan (Reth) raised whether gas reservoir and spilled gas fields should be added to trace methods.
  - Acknowledged as separate from BAL-specific JSON RPC; to be discussed async.
  - Spencer suggested PR-ing to the tracing EIP and aligning on that PR.

sections.heading: EIP-7997 Contracts Factory in EELS
sections.summary: Consensus that no irregular state transition specification is needed for EIP-7997 since the factory is already deployed; EELS PR to be closed.
sections.body:
- Toni opened an [EELS PR](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3198) to add the EIP-7997 contracts factory via an irregular state transition.
- Context: checking contract existence adds to the execution witness, causing client divergence at fork boundary.
  - Toni discovered divergence between Erigon and Geth when comparing JSON RPC responses: one had the factory deployed at fork boundary and the other did not.
- Mario Vega provided context: an [EIP PR](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/11952/changes) (already merged) removed the mention of irregular state transition from the EIP itself.
  - The EIP now says if the contract is not there, a theoretical other EIP would describe the irregular state transition, but that EIP doesn't exist because it's unnecessary.
- Marius (Geth) confirmed the team discussed this internally and concluded it's not important to specify since it will never happen on mainnet.
- Consensus: no need to specify the irregular state transition; the factory is already deployed on all relevant chains.
- Toni will close the EELS PR; confirmed nothing critical.
